concepts.def: Style emerging in mid-1950s America from rhythm and blues and country, popularised by Elvis Presley and Chuck Berry.
Detroit record label founded by Berry Gordy in 1959, releasing soul hits by The Supremes, Marvin Gaye and Stevie Wonder.
Late-1960s and 1970s style with extended forms and classical influences, exemplified by Pink Floyd and Yes.
Stripped-down, fast and aggressive style emerging 1976-77, led by the Sex Pistols and The Clash in Britain.
Genre originating in 1970s New York combining rapping, sampling, DJing and breakdancing, founded in the Bronx.
Computer-produced dance genres including house, techno and drum and bass, developing from late-1980s club culture.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 4: Popular Music and Jazz — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 4: Popular Music and Jazz brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 4: Popular Music and Jazz.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
